clips.title: Claude SDK Hooks: PreToolUse & PostToolUse | Claude Certified Architect Foundations - 05
clips.why: A focused walk through the two tool hooks, with a strong point about what a block message should say.
look: Why he says a hook is not a logger: it can change what happens next.
PreToolUse as the bouncer at the door, and what a good refusal tells the model.
Why a hook should return the refusal as data instead of throwing an error.
clips.after: Our wall returns a calm reason with an alternative, and records it, for exactly the reasons in this clip.

clips.title: Claude SDK Hooks: PreToolUse & PostToolUse | Claude Certified Architect Foundations - 05
clips.why: A short look at PostToolUse changing what the model sees after a tool ran.
look: That PostToolUse works on the tool's result, after the call already happened.
clips.after: Our PostToolUse hook does not rewrite results; it adds the linter's findings, so the model fixes them right away.

clips.title: Claude Code Permissions Explained: Why Your Allow Rule Still Fails
clips.why: Hooks next to permission rules: what each can decide, and why you often want both.
look: What a rule can see (the tool and a pattern) and what a hook can see (all the arguments).
clips.after: We keep the deny rules and add hooks on top, so a refusal is both certain and explained.

practice.q: Finish the decision a PreToolUse hook returns to refuse a call.
practice.why: deny stops the call in every permission mode, and the model reads the reason instead of the tool's output.

practice.q: You register PreToolUse: [{ matcher: "test/.*", hooks: [guard] }]. Why does guard never run for edits to test files?

options.text: Matchers are case-sensitive, so it needs "Test/.*"
options.why: Case is not the problem. The pattern is compared with something else entirely.

options.text: A matcher is compared with the tool name, not the file path
options.why: Use "Edit|Write" as the matcher and check tool_input.file_path inside the hook.

options.text: PreToolUse hooks never run for Edit
options.why: They run for every tool their matcher matches, Edit included.

practice.q: Nova tries to edit a locked test file. Put what happens in order.
items: The model asks for Edit on test/cart.test.ts
The PreToolUse hook sees the protected path and returns deny with a reason
The refusal is written to the ledger and the edit never happens
The model reads the reason and changes the product code instead
When it wants to stop, the Stop hook checks for a passing test run first
practice.why: The wall acts before the tool runs, the model gets a way forward, and the Stop hook still asks for proof at the end.

practice.q: Finish the Stop hook's guard, so a stop that follows a blocked stop is let through.
practice.hint: The input field that says a hook already blocked the last stop.
practice.why: Without it, a hook that keeps blocking could send the model round forever. The second stop is let through and recorded for people.

practice.q: Which reason keeps the model on a good path after a refused edit?

options.why: A bare refusal gives no direction. Models tend to try the same thing through another tool.

options.text: "That file is one of the checks you are judged by. Change the code, or add a new test file."
options.why: It says why and offers a better route, which is what the model needs to keep working.

options.text: No reason at all, to save tokens
options.why: The reason is the only thing the model learns from the refusal. A few words are worth it.
